title: Coral and the Bakery
premise: Theo Quintana, a lighthouse keeper's granddaughter who writes as 'he' on the page and off, has spent a decade exchanging anonymous letters with someone who signed only 'C.' When the letters stop and a stranger named Coral opens a bakery next door to his rented cottage, Theo suspects the impossible: that his pen pal has been beside him all along. As the town's Harvest-by-the-Sea festival approaches, Theo must decide whether to keep lending pieces of himself to fiction or risk the whole heart in real life. The story ends at the festival's closing bonfire, where Theo confesses he was the writer all along, and Coral admits she stopped writing because she'd fallen for him first.
about_author: L. M. Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent years cataloguing lighthouse logs along the Atlantic coast before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who say true things in letters and false things in person.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. On the anniversary of ten years of correspondence, Theo rereads the final unsigned letter from 'C.'—abrupt, unfinished—and drafts a reply he never sends. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as routine, establishing how much of Theo's inner life lives on paper.

chapters.title: Salt and Flour
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral arrives in Harborlight to open a bakery in her late aunt's building, carrying a shoebox of letters she has never had the courage to sign. She meets her new neighbor without realizing who he is. Beat: hope tangled with fear of being known.

chapters.title: Next Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo brings a housewarming loaf back to the bakery (a mistake—he bought it there) and is disarmed by Coral's laugh, which sounds like handwriting he knows. He says too little and leaves too fast. Beat: recognition he refuses to name.

chapters.title: What the Lighthouse Keeps
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits his grandmother's decommissioned lighthouse, now a museum, and tells the docent stories about the letters while avoiding the truth of why they ended. Flashback reveals the letters began after his mother left. Beat: memory as both shelter and cage.

chapters.title: Closing Time Conversations
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral and Theo fall into an easy rhythm of end-of-day talks over her counter. She almost shows him the shoebox, then hides it when he mentions his pen pal wistfully. Beat: intimacy growing on borrowed identity.

chapters.title: The Festival Committee
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The town ropes them both into organizing the Harvest-by-the-Sea festival—Theo on posters, Coral on food. Their bickering turns flirtatious in front of the whole committee. Beat: public chemistry, private panic.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral notices ink stains on Theo's hands matching the letters' pen, and a phrase he says aloud that exists word-for-word in letter forty-three. She convinces herself it's coincidence. Beat: suspicion sharpening into longing.

chapters.title: A Storm Makes Cowards of Us All
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A gale knocks out power; Coral's freezer stock is at risk. Theo helps her save the dough through the night by lamplight, and they nearly kiss before a fuse blows. Beat: closeness interrupted by his own retreat.

chapters.title: The Unsent Reply
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finally mails the decade-late reply to 'C.,' addressed to a PO box long closed, and tells himself the door is shut. His editor rejects his novel draft for having 'a heart kept offstage.' Beat: art mirroring avoidance.

chapters.title: Rye Bread and Bad Excuses
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tests Theo with details from the letters—a fake memory of a shared book. Theo corrects her with the exact edition and margin note. She walks home shaking. Beat: certainty arriving before courage does.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Trunk
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Sorting his grandmother's belongings, Theo finds her own bundle of letters—to a sailor who never came back—and understands what a lifetime of unsent words costs. Beat: generational warning, resolve forming.

chapters.title: Almost Told You
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the pier, each nearly confesses—their dialogue overlapping, missing, colliding. Coral says 'I know you,' Theo hears it as friendship. Both leave wounded by the near-miss. Beat: dramatic irony at its tightest.

chapters.title: The Rival Recipe
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A chain café offers to buy Coral out, threatening the bakery and her reason to stay. Theo defends her fiercely at the town meeting, revealing feelings publicly. Beat: stakes widen beyond romance to belonging.

chapters.title: Pieces on Loan
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo rewrites his novel in one fevered night, making the heroine a baker and the hero a coward. He titles a chapter 'Coral.' Beat: truth migrating from life into art, and the shame that follows.

chapters.title: She Reads the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral finds the printed draft in his cottage while returning a casserole dish, reads three pages, and recognizes their entire correspondence refracted. She puts it down unread further and flees. Beat: betrayal and heartbreak braided together.

chapters.title: Cold Counter, Cold Shoulder
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Coral goes distant; the bakery's blinds stay down. Theo, oblivious to why, spirals into old self-protection, deciding some doors are meant to stay shut. Beat: lowest point, the wound self-inflicted twice over.

chapters.title: The Docent's Story
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The lighthouse docent reveals Coral has been visiting weekly, asking about the keeper's granddaughter who wrote letters. Theo realizes she's known longer than he has—and came anyway. Beat: reversal, hope reignited.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral unpacks the shoebox at last, rereading every letter, and writes a new one signing her full name. She plans to read it aloud at the festival if he doesn't speak first. Beat: courage assembled from ten years of evidence.

chapters.title: Harvest-by-the-Sea
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The festival blooms—lanterns, the bakery's stall mobbed, Theo's poster everywhere. They orbit each other all day, each waiting for the other, tension stretched to snapping. Beat: the held breath before the climax.

chapters.title: The Bonfire Confession
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the closing bonfire, Theo takes the stage during the storytelling hour and reads his chapter 'Coral' aloud, admitting he is C.'s correspondent and has been a coward in person. Beat: climax—risking the whole heart in public.

chapters.title: Signed, Finally
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral answers by reading her own letter—signed at last—then kissing him amid the crowd's cheer. They trade confessions: why she stopped writing, why he hid. Beat: release, the letters' decade resolved in minutes.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Spring: the bakery thrives, the novel sells with its heart onstage, and a new letter sits framed above the counter—the first they wrote to each other face to face. Beat: found family, chosen identity, second chances kept.
